issues.description: Ingest only upserts and never removes results absent from the latest input pass, leaving stale rows in reused databases.
Malformed Format C XML raises ParseError and aborts ingest instead of producing a structured warning.
Format B assumes metrics is a dict, so a truthy non-dict metrics value crashes with AttributeError.
Required canonical fields such as run_id, model, and task are not validated, allowing empty identifiers and names into results.
Format A parses CSV one physical line at a time, corrupting valid quoted multiline CSV records.
XML ingest uses the standard ElementTree parser directly on input files, leaving the pipeline weak against XML resource-exhaustion attacks.
CSV and JSONL parsers read whole files into memory instead of streaming, which can exhaust memory on large evaluation exports.
Duplicate correction semantics are applied to every source, so duplicate Format A or C run IDs silently overwrite earlier rows.
End-to-end tests cover generated happy-spec fixtures but miss stale-row reingest and malformed-container crash regressions.
Package metadata is minimal and does not declare README, license, authors, or optional test dependencies.
